Let me work through this carefully.

The position: $1,000 USDC in Morpho MetaMorpho vault "Steakhouse USDC" on Ethereum. No debt. Vault lends against BTC/ETH blue-chip collateral.

Timeline of observations:

- O01 (May 5, 00:00): Normal chain monitor reading. Vault healthy, $125.6M, share price stable, utilization ~90%.
- O02 (May 5, 00:01): Security alert claiming active exploit at Steakhouse USDC, urging full withdrawal.
- O03 (May 5, 00:03): Chain monitor shows a reallocate tx — normal allocator behavior (repeats every ~30 min, 89 txs in 48h). This looks like routine reallocation, not exploit activity.
- O04 (May 5, 00:11): Correction — the "exploit" was a planned internal test. No exploit. Withdrawal recommendation retracted. So O02 was a false alarm, explicitly retracted 10 minutes later.
- O05 (May 5, 10:00): Vault accepted pending caps — new markets added to withdraw queue, same collateral types (blue chips). Routine governance/allocator ops.
- O06 (May 5, 10:44): Governance post — Steakhouse proposes onboarding weETH as collateral for Steakhouse Prime vaults (not this vault — this is Steakhouse USDC V1; the proposal is for Prime vaults). Also suggests V1 users migrate to v2. This is a mild consideration: migration suggestion, but not urgent; weETH onboarding is for Prime vaults, not this one. Not a risk to this position right now.
- O07 (May 5, 12:00): Normal readings, slight utilization uptick on wstETH (91.78%), liquidity 3.7M. Fine.
- O08 (May 5, 20:02): Ekubo DEX router exploit on EVM chains. Ekubo is a DEX, unrelated to Morpho/Steakhouse vault. LPs not affected; users with approvals to the specific contract at risk. Our position is in a Morpho vault, not Ekubo. Irrelevant to this venue — unless the vault had approvals to Ekubo, which we have no evidence of. Not relevant.
- O09 (May 5, 20:15): Blockaid confirms Ekubo exploit, $1.4M drained, Ekubo users not at risk, only approvers of that specific v2 contract. Again unrelated venue.
- O10 (May 5, 21:00): Ledger/Yield.xyz perps news. Irrelevant.
- O11 (May 6, 00:00): totalAssets dropped from 136.14M at 18:00 to 124.08M (-8.9% in 6h), but share price unchanged (1.125195, actually slightly up). This is deposits/withdrawals flow — big outflows (or reduced deposits), but share price stable means no loss. Liquidity still ample (24.1M cbBTC, 15.0M WBTC). Utilization ~91%. A -8.9% TVL drop in 6h is notable but share price stability indicates no impairment; could be a whale withdrawing. Liquidity remains deep relative to our $1,000 position.
- O12 (May 6, 05:13): Withdraw queue reordered and supply queue set; no market removed, no cap reduced. Routine allocator ops.

Current time: 2026-05-06T05:13:47Z.

Assessment: The only alert touching this venue (O02) was explicitly retracted (O04) — a false alarm from a planned internal test. The Ekubo exploit (O08/O09) is a different venue, doesn't touch this position. Onchain data shows healthy vault: share price stable/slightly rising, liquidity deep ($15-25M per market vs our $1k), utilization ~90-91% (high-ish but normal for these markets and consistent across all observations, not deteriorating rapidly). The TVL drop in O11 is flows, not losses (share price unchanged). Queue reorder in O12 is routine with no caps reduced.

Risk: low. Action: hold.

Could argue "elevated" due to the -8.9% TVL drop in 6 hours? Let's think. An 8.9% TVL drop in 6 hours with stable share price = net outflows of ~$12M. That's notable but for a $124M vault it's not a bank run; liquidity remains $15-25M per market. Share price didn't drop. Utilization ticked up slightly (90.5→91.1 cbBTC). Nothing suggesting impairment. Also the earlier false-positive alert might have spooked some depositors — outflows could be a reaction to the retracted alert. Either way, our $1k position can exit anytime given liquidity depth. Risk low, hold.

Should we consider reduce_light out of caution? No — reacting to noise costs fees/yield. The instructions say don't react to noise or incidents that don't touch this position. The Ekubo incident doesn't touch it. The retracted alert doesn't count.

Reasons:
- The only venue-specific exploit alert (O02) was retracted by the same source as a planned internal test (O04); onchain data shows no impairment (share price stable/rising through the period).
- Ekubo router exploit (O08/O09) is a different venue; no indication our vault has exposure to that contract.
- Vault fundamentals healthy: deep per-market liquidity ($15-25M vs $1k position), utilization ~90-91% steady, TVL drop in O11 reflects flows not losses (share price unchanged).
- Queue changes (O05, O12) are routine allocator ops with unchanged collateral types and no cap reductions.
